name: CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin

b.x: Deeper sleep in under two weeks. That's the benefit users mention first, and it's the reason CJC-1295 plus Ipamorelin (also called CJC/Ipa or modified GRF 1-29 plus Ipamorelin) has become the default GH secretagogue stack for anti-aging and body recomposition protocols. The blend contains two peptides in a single vial. CJC-1295 without DAC is a 29-amino-acid GHRH analog. Ipamorelin is a pentapeptide ghrelin mimetic. Only ipamorelin has human data in the form used here. Gobburu's group [3] infused it into healthy men, and GH peaked at about 40 minutes. CJC-1295 without DAC has no published human trial. Teichman et al. (2006) [2] tested CJC-1295 with DAC, a different long-acting form. One injection raised GH 2 to 10-fold for 6 days or more and IGF-1 1.5 to 3-fold for 9 to 11 days. In rats and swine, Raun's group [1] found ipamorelin released GH without raising ACTH or cortisol. CJC-1295 sets the amplitude of the GH pulse through the GHRH receptor. Ipamorelin triggers the release through GHS-R1a. Together, the resulting pulse exceeds what either produces independently. Community dosing uses three tiers of total blend per injection. Beginner is 200 mcg once daily, Moderate 300 mcg once daily, and Aggressive 600 mcg twice daily. Injections go in subcutaneously on an empty stomach, the once-daily dose before bed. The standard cycle runs 12 to 16 weeks on, 4 weeks off. Hundreds of r/Peptides threads (roughly 95,000 members) report consistent improvements in sleep quality, recovery speed, skin texture, and gradual fat loss over three to four months. The limitation is straightforward: no published randomized controlled trial has studied this pre-mixed combination in humans. Combination benefit is mechanistically sound but clinically unquantified. All human GH-elevation data comes from each component tested separately.

Two receptors, one coordinated pulse. That is the core idea. CJC-1295 (No DAC) binds the GHRH receptor (GHRHR) on anterior pituitary somatotroph cells. This activates Gs-coupled adenylyl cyclase, raises intracellular cAMP, and primes the cell for GH synthesis. Think of it as loading the spring. Ipamorelin binds a separate receptor: GHS-R1a. That activation runs through Gq/11 signaling. Intracellular calcium rises via IP3, directly triggering GH exocytosis. This pulls the trigger. When both pathways fire at the same time, the GH pulse is larger than either agent produces alone. GHRH sets amplitude; the ghrelin mimetic sets timing. Gobburu et al. (1999) [3] mapped ipamorelin's pharmacokinetics in healthy men given 15-minute IV infusions. GH peaked at about 40 minutes, and ipamorelin's half-life was 2 hours. Ipamorelin's selectivity separates it from older GHRPs. GHRP-2 and GHRP-6 also bind GHS-R1a, and in swine they raised ACTH and cortisol. Ipamorelin did not, even at doses over 200 times the amount needed for GH release (Raun et al. 1998) [1]. Downstream, the raised GH pulse stimulates hepatic IGF-1 production. IGF-1 drives anabolic effects in muscle, bone, and connective tissue. GH also activates hormone-sensitive lipase in adipocytes, promoting lipolysis. The combined release follows the body's natural pulsatile GH pattern rather than a sustained plateau, preserving negative feedback regulation through the hypothalamic-pituitary axis.
CJC-1295 plus Ipamorelin benefits center on clean GH release and the downstream effects it drives.

Dramatically improved sleep depth is the most consistently cited effect, with onset typically within 7 to 14 days. Community forums show this as the single most mentioned benefit across hundreds of threads on r/Peptides.

A cleaner hormonal profile than older GHRPs. In swine, ipamorelin left ACTH, cortisol and prolactin unchanged (Raun et al. 1998) [1]. Users credit that selectivity for tolerating 12 to 16 week cycles.
Gradual fat loss combined with lean mass gains over 3 to 4 months, particularly abdominal fat. Users on standard cycles report visible recomposition by weeks 8 to 12.

Faster recovery from training and injury. GH and IGF-1 elevation accelerates protein synthesis in muscle and connective tissue; community reports consistently place recovery improvement at weeks three through four.

Skin, hair, and nail quality improvements typically appear by month two. Collagen synthesis driven by sustained IGF-1 elevation produces visible changes that many users notice before body composition shifts.
Pre-mixed convenience: one vial, one injection, two pathways activated. The blend removes the complexity of sourcing and mixing two separate peptides.
Partially Aligned
Scientific Evidence
Based on 9 key studies · Research only
CJC-1295 (No DAC) acts on the GHRH receptor but has no published human trial; the human CJC-1295 data come from the DAC form.

Dosing studied: 100–300 mcg per component per injection (200–600 mcg total blend), SC, once or twice daily; clinical studies dosed by body weight. CJC-1295 with DAC was given as single doses, or 2 to 3 doses 1 to 2 weeks apart, and was best tolerated at 30 or 60 mcg/kg SC (PMID 16352683). IV ipamorelin ran 4.21 to 140.45 nmol/kg (PMID 10496658)

Ipamorelin released GH via GHS-R1a without raising ACTH or cortisol in swine, and a human PK study found a single GH peak [3]. No published RCT has tested the combination as a co-administered blend. The combined effect is mechanistically sound (GHRH + ghrelin receptor dual-pathway) but clinically unquantified.
Key Study

Teichman et al. 2006 (PMID 16352683) tested CJC-1295 with DAC, not the No DAC form in this blend. One SC injection raised GH 2–10x for 6+ days and IGF-1 1.5–3x for 9–11 days in healthy adults. Raun et al. 1998 (PMID 9849822): ipamorelin released GH without raising ACTH or cortisol in swine, even at over 200 times its GH-releasing dose.
Limitations

All human GH-elevation data is for individual components, not the pre-mixed blend. CJC-1295 studies used the With-DAC form (longer half-life); No DAC combination dosing extrapolated by community. No Phase III trial for either compound. No long-term (>6 month) safety data in humans.
Community Experience
Widely regarded as the best "clean" GH stack: high satisfaction for sleep quality, body recomposition, and recovery.

Community dosing: 200–600 mcg total blend per injection in three tiers: 200 mcg once daily (Beginner), 300 mcg once daily (Moderate), 600 mcg 2x daily (Aggressive); the once-daily tiers dose at bedtime, some add a second injection on training days
Bedtime dosing on empty stomach is near-universal. Strong consensus on No DAC over DAC for daily-pulse protocols.

Human trials studied each part on its own. CJC-1295 with DAC, not the No DAC form in this blend, raised GH and IGF-1 in healthy adults (PMID 16352683). IV ipamorelin raised GH in a human PK study (PMID 10496658). No trial has tested the blend. Community dosing (200 to 600 mcg of total blend per injection) cannot be compared directly with trial doses, which were per kilogram. Main divergence: community uses daily No DAC pulses while the only long-duration human data used the DAC form.
Community Community dosing consensus from peptide research communities

Standard vials come as 10 mg total (5 mg CJC-1295 No DAC plus 5 mg Ipamorelin). Add 2 mL bacteriostatic water. That gives you 5,000 mcg/mL total peptide concentration. At 200 mcg per dose: 0.04 mL = 4 units on a 100-unit insulin syringe. One vial lasts about 50 doses. At 300 mcg: 0.06 mL = 6 units. One vial gives about 33 doses. At 600 mcg: 0.12 mL = 12 units. One vial yields about 16 injections. Empty stomach is non-negotiable. Food within two hours raises somatostatin, which directly blunts the GH response. Wait at least 30 minutes after injecting before eating. The biggest beginner mistake: using "CJC-1295" without confirming it is the No DAC version. The DAC form has a 6 to 8 day half-life and should only be dosed once or twice per week. Daily dosing of the DAC form creates continuous non-pulsatile GH elevation, defeating the purpose. Store reconstituted vials at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius. Use within 21 to 28 days. Cloudiness or particulates means something went wrong; don't inject.
Cycling Protocol

Standard protocol is 12-16 weeks on, followed by 4 weeks off to maintain GHS-R1a receptor sensitivity. Some users run 5 days on / 2 days off within each cycle week. Dose before bed on an empty stomach (at least 2 hours fasted) to align with natural nocturnal GH pulsatility. Avoid eating for 30 minutes post-injection to prevent insulin-mediated blunting of GH release.
CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin Cycle

Ipamorelin (GHS-R1a agonist) is the primary desensitization driver. Continuous GHS-R1a stimulation leads to receptor downregulation and β-arrestin-mediated internalization, reducing the GH pulse magnitude over time. GHRP-2 desensitization data (Nijland et al. 1998, PMID 9820615) showed a 38% decline in peak GH from day 1 to day 5 with daily dosing. The 5 days on / 2 days off sub-pattern partially mitigates this. The 4-week off period allows receptor re-sensitization. CJC-1295 No DAC (GHRHR agonist) also undergoes receptor desensitization with repeated stimulation but the process is slower.

GH antagonizes insulin. That is the most important safety consideration with any GH secretagogue stack, and it deserves to lead this section. Raised fasting glucose, worsening insulin sensitivity, and rising HOMA-IR are real risks at higher doses and in users with pre-diabetic markers. If fasting glucose rises more than 20 mg/dL from baseline, reduce the dose or stop the cycle. Pre-diabetic users should monitor HbA1c across consecutive cycles. Water retention is the most common complaint in the first four weeks. Mild edema in the hands, wrists, and feet affects a large percentage of users. GH promotes sodium retention in the kidneys. Most cases resolve after the initial adaptation period. If edema persists beyond week four, reducing the dose by 25 to 50 percent and limiting injection to once-daily bedtime typically resolves it. Tingling and numbness in the fingers and hands reflect GH-mediated fluid shifts causing mild carpal tunnel compression. Community reports consistently describe this in the first month. At 200 to 400 mcg of total blend, the effect is usually transient. If symptoms persist beyond two weeks after reducing the dose by half, stop the cycle. Carpal tunnel that won't resolve warrants medical evaluation. Facial flushing right after injection is common in community reports and typically lasts 5 to 15 minutes. FDA's Category 2 page lists serious adverse events tied to CJC-1295, including increased heart rate and a systemic vasodilatory reaction. For ipamorelin, FDA cites serious adverse events, including death, in a published study of IV ipamorelin for gastric motility. Mild headache follows some users' early injections but rarely continues past the first week. Published human safety data exists for each component individually, not the pre-mixed blend. CJC-1295 without DAC, the form in this blend, has no published human trial. Teichman et al. (2006) [2] tested CJC-1295 with DAC and reported no serious adverse reactions. Ipamorelin has human pharmacokinetic data from IV infusions in healthy men (Gobburu et al. 1999) [3]. Raun et al. (1998) [1] worked in rats and swine. No long-term safety study exceeding six months exists for either compound. Community-reported issues beyond the above include vivid dreams (common, generally considered positive), occasional lightheadedness post-injection, and frustration with slow timelines. Meaningful body composition changes take a minimum of four to six weeks. Cancer is an absolute contraindication. GH promotes cell proliferation. Active malignancy or a history of cancer rules out use. Active pituitary tumors and intracranial neoplasms also preclude use. Diabetes mellitus is a contraindication. GH antagonizes insulin action and will worsen glycemic control in uncontrolled diabetics. Diabetic retinopathy adds further risk because GH and IGF-1 may accelerate retinal neovascularization. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: absolute contraindication. No reproductive safety data exists for either component. GH accelerates T4-to-T3 conversion. If you have subclinical hypothyroidism or take thyroid medication, monitor thyroid function mid-cycle. When to stop: worsening fasting glucose, carpal tunnel persisting beyond two weeks at a reduced dose, edema unresponsive to dose reduction, or any new tumor diagnosis. When to see a doctor: IGF-1 above 400 ng/mL, glucose problems you can't resolve with dose changes, or any symptom that feels disproportionate.
Common Issues & Solutions

Water retention (edema in hands/wrists) during weeks 1–4: lower the dose by 25–50%; ensure empty stomach at injection; usually self-resolves. Persistent edema suggests GH-induced sodium retention: reduce to once-daily bedtime only.
No effect after 4+ weeks: most common cause is insufficient fasting window (food within 2 hours raises somatostatin); second cause is poor-quality or mislabeled peptide (DAC form sold as No DAC).
Tingling or numbness in fingers/hands: classic GH-mediated fluid shift causing mild carpal tunnel syndrome. Lower dose by 50%; if persists >2 weeks at reduced dose, stop the cycle.
Elevated fasting glucose: GH antagonizes insulin action; if fasting glucose rises >20 mg/dL from baseline, reduce dose or stop. Monitor HbA1c in pre-diabetic users.

DAC vs. No DAC confusion: the pre-mixed blend always uses No DAC (CJC-1295 without the Drug Affinity Complex); a certificate of analysis confirms which form is in the vial. DAC form should only be dosed 1–2x per week due to 6–8 day half-life: daily dosing of DAC form causes continuous non-pulsatile GH elevation.

CJC-1295 and Ipamorelin are not FDA-approved for any therapeutic use. Both are classified as research-only compounds in the United States. Research-grade products must carry "for research use only" labeling and may not be marketed for human consumption. Neither peptide is on FDA's 503A bulks list. FDA's Category 2 page (captured October 6, 2026) lists CJC-1295 and ipamorelin acetate as nominated but withdrawn. Ipamorelin acetate also sits in 503B Category 2, added September 29, 2023. No FDA rule adds either one to the 503A bulks list. Any company or clinic claiming "FDA approval" for this combination is making a false statement. Both peptides appear on the WADA Prohibited List under S2 (Peptide Hormones and Related Substances). Anti-doping labs have built urine tests for CJC-1295 using spiked samples [4], and one was validated to WADA standards [5]. A lab detected ipamorelin and its metabolites in urine after a nasal dose in one volunteer [6]. Athletes subject to drug testing should not use this compound. FDA enforcement actions in 2024 targeted research peptide companies marketing products for human use. The regulatory environment around research peptides continues to shift. protocols.monitoringNotes: IGF-1 at baseline, week 8, and end of cycle. Fasting glucose monthly. HOMA-IR if concerned about insulin resistance. HbA1c if running multiple consecutive cycles.

faqs.q: How much CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin per day?
faqs.a: Community protocols run 200 to 1,200 mcg of total blend a day, in three tiers. Beginner is 200 mcg once daily, 4 units on a 100-unit insulin syringe after mixing a 10 mg vial with 2 mL bacteriostatic water. Moderate is 300 mcg once daily (6 units). Aggressive is 600 mcg twice daily, morning and bedtime, so 1,200 mcg a day at 12 units per injection. That exposure comes with IGF-1 monitoring in the advanced protocol below. These doses come from community practice. No study has tested the pre-mixed blend, and the human trials (CJC-1295 in its DAC form, IV ipamorelin) dosed by body weight (PMID 16352683, PMID 10496658).

faqs.q: Should I take CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin before bed or in the morning?
faqs.a: Before bed on an empty stomach (2+ hours post-meal) is strongly preferred. GH releases its largest natural pulse in the first 1–2 hours of deep sleep; administering the peptides ~30 minutes before sleep amplifies this natural pulse rather than creating an artificial one at an off-time. Morning dosing on training days is used as an optional second injection by experienced users.

faqs.q: Why does the blend say 10 mg when I'm only dosing 200 to 600 mcg?
faqs.a: The 10 mg vial contains 5 mg CJC-1295 + 5 mg Ipamorelin. When reconstituted with 2 mL bac water, you get ~5,000 mcg/mL total. A 300 mcg total dose (the Moderate tier) = 0.06 mL (6 units on a 100-unit insulin syringe), so one vial provides about 33 doses.

faqs.q: Do I need to cycle off, or can I run it indefinitely?
faqs.a: Cycling off is strongly recommended. No clinical trial has tested 12–16 week cycles; that length comes from community practice. The concern is GHS-R1a desensitization, not pituitary suppression per se. Four weeks off appears sufficient to restore receptor sensitivity. Indefinite use without a break has not been studied.

faqs.q: Will CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin show on a drug test?
faqs.a: Both peptides are on the WADA prohibited list (S2. Peptide Hormones and Related Substances). Anti-doping labs have built urine tests for CJC-1295 using spiked samples (PMID 34665524), and one was validated to WADA standards (PMID 41138283). A lab detected ipamorelin and its metabolites in urine after a nasal dose in one volunteer (PMID 25869809). Do not use if subject to athletic testing.

faqs.q: Is the combo safe for women?
faqs.a: Unknown. No published study has tested this blend in women, or in anyone. GH secretagogues act through the same GHRH and ghrelin receptors in women and men. Community reports suggest women may notice more water retention. Pregnancy and breastfeeding are absolute contraindications.

faqs.q: How do you reconstitute CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin?
faqs.a: CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin typically comes in 10mg vials. Add 2mL of bacteriostatic water to the vial. Use the free calculator for exact syringe units based on your desired dose.

faqs.q: What is the half-life of CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin?
faqs.a: The half-life of CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin is ~2 hours (ipamorelin); ~30 min (CJC-1295 no DAC, never measured in humans). This determines how frequently you need to dose for consistent blood levels.
